card.law_is_about: Limiting health-insurance spending, including volume-related reductions in reimbursement for digital health applications (DiGA).
card.they_want: Reject additional price controls for DiGA.
card.they_claim: DiGA enter care only after a positive healthcare effect has been demonstrated.
card.the_problem: Lower-risk DiGA may be admitted and reimbursed provisionally while the required effect is still being tested. Permanent admission requires the evidence.

counter_quote.original: Für DiGA niedriger Risikoklassen ist eine vorläufige Aufnahme zur Erprobung möglich, wenn der Nutzen noch nicht belegt ist.
counter_quote.translation_en: Translation: For lower-risk DiGA, provisional admission for testing is possible when the benefit has not yet been demonstrated.

correction: Distinguish permanent admission from provisional admission for testing. Section 139e(4) permits lower-risk DiGA to enter the reimbursable directory when the positive-effect evidence is not yet available, subject to other requirements, a plausible rationale and an independent evaluation plan. Permanent admission requires the positive-effect evidence. The general statement that care starts only after demonstration omits an affirmative statutory route to earlier reimbursed care.
effect: Qualifies the premise that all reimbursed DiGA already have a demonstrated positive effect. It weakens that part of the argument that further reimbursement controls would penalise established beneficial care, but does not determine whether the proposed volume reductions are appropriate.
limits: Provisional admission is regulated and requires safety, quality, data-protection and evaluation conditions; it is not unrestricted marketing. Missing final evidence is not proof that a particular DiGA is ineffective, unsafe or fails to help patients. No clinical outcome, actual effect size, manufacturer cost or optimal reimbursement price is established. No intent is inferred.
context_and_alternatives: The full 37-page author submission was read. Its DiGA section occupies physical 32–34 and links claimed demonstrated benefit to opposition to quantity-related reimbursement reductions. It also offers independent cost, access, demographic and innovation arguments.

The strongest benign reading is a shorthand description of permanent admission or of the longer-term duty to demonstrate benefit. That reading fits established permanently admitted applications but is not stated: the printed sentence describes entry into care generally and includes no permanent-admission restriction. The finding is confined to that universal description, not the author's expertise or all DiGA arguments.

The pre-submission GKV statutory report expressly distinguishes lower-risk provisional admission from higher-risk IIb applications that must provide evidence at entry. Its introduction was read together with foreword and executive-summary context. The author cites that same 2025 report later on physical 34, describing it as March 2026; the PDF imprint says 1 April 2026. That small publication-month mismatch is not a separate finding.

Current §139e(2) and(4) were checked as corroboration, not used to assume a later rule applied before the statement. The addressed draft amends prices in §134 without eliminating provisional admission. BfArM guideline retrieval failed 403, so no independent full guideline read is claimed.

The separate 43-percent physician-age figure is not alleged erroneous: the term niedergelassen can denote practice owners, and primary BAEK figures around 43–44 percent for owners provide a strong denominator rescue. Homeopathy evidence-quality and cost-effectiveness disagreements are also not treated as proven factual errors.
materiality_explanation: Minor: the statement overgeneralises a relevant evidential safeguard, but established permanently admitted DiGA do have to demonstrate positive effects and the author advances multiple independent objections to price cuts. No false clinical efficacy conclusion is inferred.
direction_explanation: True for this rationale: presenting demonstrated benefit as universal at entry makes additional controls appear to penalise beneficial care, supporting the express request to reject them. This direction assessment is separate from minor severity.

confidence.text_source_mismatch: High for the unqualified entry description versus the express provisional route; permanent-admission shorthand remains a benign explanation.
